title: Modest global food-security gains coexist with high healthy-diet costs, regional disparities, and unequal nutrition exposure
source_unit: FAO, IFAD, UNICEF, WFP, and WHO, The State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World 2026
geography: Global and regional food insecurity, diet quality, nutrition, and healthy-diet affordability estimates

observations.period: 2025; global hunger and food insecurity estimates

denominator.unit: world population and global food-insecurity estimation frame

hunger_prevalence.unit: percent of the world population affected by hunger

moderate_or_severe_food_insecurity.unit: billion people experiencing moderate or severe food insecurity

direction.value: global food security and nutrition improved modestly in 2025

target_gap.value: progress remains uneven and insufficient to meet 2030 targets

observations.method: UN system global and regional estimates of hunger, food insecurity, diet quality, and nutrition indicators.
observations.uncertainty: These are modeled and harmonized population estimates, not respondent-level nutrition histories or household food diaries; definitions, survey coverage, and revisions affect comparability.
observations.subgroup: People experiencing hunger or food insecurity, low-income households, children, women, rural communities, and populations in regions with slower progress.
observations.counterinterpretation: A modest global improvement can reflect meaningful policy and food-system gains even while the level of unmet need remains exceptionally high.

denominator.unit: global and regional SDG 2 progress frame

africa_direction.value: first signs of improvement in Africa since adoption of the 2030 Agenda

regional_disparity.value: global progress remains uneven, with persistent regional differences in hunger and nutrition outcomes

policy_signal.value: regional improvement does not remove the need for coordinated food-system, social-protection, and nutrition policy

observations.method: Comparative regional estimates and cross-country synthesis across food security, diet quality, and nutrition targets.
observations.uncertainty: Regional aggregates conceal within-country, rural-urban, gender, age, conflict, and income differences; they do not identify individual causal pathways.
observations.subgroup: Residents of Africa and other slower-progress regions, rural communities, women, young children, and households exposed to conflict or high food costs.
observations.counterinterpretation: Regional improvement can provide a platform for scaling effective interventions, infrastructure, and public investment rather than implying that disparities are fixed.

denominator.unit: global healthy-diet affordability and food-cost assessment frame

access_constraint.value: healthy diets remain out of reach for billions

africa_unaffordability.unit: approximate share of people in Africa unable to afford a healthy diet

structural_drivers.value: food prices, incomes, food-system structure, and economic conditions shape healthy-diet access

consumer_tradeoff.value: limited affordability can push households toward less nutritious foods even when aggregate food availability improves

observations.method: Healthy-diet cost and affordability analysis linked to food-security and nutrition estimates.
observations.uncertainty: Affordability thresholds are constructed estimates and do not measure each household's actual purchases, preferences, preparation time, or intra-household allocation.
observations.subgroup: Low-income consumers, food-insecure households, women, children, rural communities, and people facing high local food prices.
observations.counterinterpretation: Income growth, lower structural costs, better distribution, social protection, and nutrition-sensitive policy can expand healthy-diet access without requiring identical diets everywhere.

observations.period: 2026; unequal nutrition exposure and policy response

denominator.unit: global nutrition-disparity and multisector policy frame

persistent_disparities.value: disparities remain particularly important for women, young children, and rural communities

diet_quality.value: diet quality continues to lag worldwide

response.value: coordinated, multisectoral action is needed to reduce structural costs, strengthen food systems, and improve equitable access

system_link.value: nutrition outcomes connect household purchasing room with agriculture, markets, health, social protection, and public investment

observations.method: Cross-sector synthesis of food insecurity, diet quality, nutrition targets, affordability, and policy levers.
observations.uncertainty: The report identifies population-level patterns and policy levers; it does not establish a single causal effect for any specific intervention or household.
observations.subgroup: Women, young children, rural communities, food-insecure households, farmers, food-system workers, health systems, and public agencies.
observations.counterinterpretation: Targeted public action and local adaptation can reduce unequal exposure even where global food prices and supply conditions remain volatile.

related_sources.claim: FAO provides the joint SOFI publication and related food-security evidence.
WHO provides complementary nutrition and malnutrition context.

boundary: This record adds a global hunger, food-insecurity, healthy-diet affordability, nutrition-disparity, and public-response route. It uses aggregate UN estimates and report synthesis, not respondent-level nutrition data, household food diaries, individual medical histories, causal food-price estimates, or proof that global hunger improvement means secure or healthy diets for every subgroup.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official WHO SOFI 2026 publication page reviewed for the title, date, joint UN production, global hunger and food-insecurity estimates, regional divergence, healthy-diet affordability, subgroup disparities, and policy framing.
